chapters.1.summary: David is back in Ziklag when a man arrives from Saul’s camp. The man is an Amalekite, and he carries Saul’s crown and bracelet. He says the wounded Saul asked him for a final blow. David and his men tear their clothes and fast until evening. David has the man put to death for killing the LORD’s anointed. Then David sings a lament for Saul and Jonathan. Three times it cries, “How the mighty have fallen!” He orders the people of Judah to learn it.
chapters.1.lds: The older Church manual says the messenger lied about killing Saul. On what evidence does David sentence him in verse 16?
chapters.2.summary: David asks the LORD and moves to Hebron. The men of Judah anoint him king there. He thanks Jabesh Gilead for burying Saul. Abner, Saul’s general, makes Saul’s son Ishbosheth king over the other tribes. The two armies meet at the pool of Gibeon. A contest of twelve against twelve turns into a battle. Joab’s brother Asahel chases Abner, ignores two warnings, and is killed. At sunset Abner calls for a halt, and Joab stops the pursuit.
chapters.2.lds: Why does Abner ask Joab to stop the fighting?
chapters.3.summary: The war between Saul’s house and David’s house lasts a long time. Ishbosheth accuses Abner over one of Saul’s concubines. Abner is furious and offers to bring all Israel to David. David first demands Michal back, and her husband follows her weeping. Abner meets David and leaves in peace. Joab calls him back and stabs him at the gate for Asahel’s death. David curses Joab’s house and leads the mourning for Abner. He says Zeruiah’s sons are too hard for him.
chapters.3.lds: What happens to Michal and her husband when David demands her return?
chapters.4.summary: Ishbosheth loses courage when he hears Abner is dead. Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth is mentioned; he was lamed as a child in the flight. Two of Ishbosheth’s captains, Rechab and Baanah, enter his house at noon. They kill him on his bed and cut off his head. They carry it all night to David at Hebron. They say the LORD has avenged David on Saul’s family. David recalls the messenger he executed at Ziklag. He has the two men killed and buries the head in Abner’s tomb.
chapters.4.lds: Why does David punish men who expect a reward for killing his rival?
chapters.5.summary: All the tribes come to Hebron and anoint David king over Israel. He is thirty years old and reigns forty years in all. He captures the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites. Jerusalem becomes the City of David. Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to build him a house. David takes more wives and has more children. The Philistines attack twice in the Valley of Rephaim. Each time David asks the LORD and wins.
chapters.5.lds: Come, Follow Me studies seeking divine guidance. For whose sake does verse 12 say the kingdom was raised up?
chapters.6.summary: David gathers thirty thousand men to bring the ark to Jerusalem. They carry it on a new cart, and Uzzah touches it and dies. David is angry and afraid and leaves it at Obed-Edom’s house. The LORD blesses that house for three months. David then brings the ark up with sacrifices, dancing in a linen ephod. Saul’s daughter Michal watches from a window and despises him. He blesses the people and gives everyone food. Michal mocks his display, and she has no child to her death.
chapters.6.lds: The older manual connects the ark’s handling with sacred responsibility. Its proposed motives are interpretations. What does Michal object to in verse 20?
chapters.7.summary: David lives in a cedar house and wants to build one for the ark. The prophet Nathan first tells him to go ahead. That night the LORD sends Nathan back with a different word. The LORD never asked for a house of cedar. He took David from the pasture and will make David a house. A son will build the temple, and his throne will last forever. If he sins he will be disciplined, but not rejected like Saul. David sits before the LORD and asks, “Who am I?”
chapters.7.lds: Come, Follow Me connects the promised house with Jesus Christ. Who will build a house for whom in verses 11–13?
chapters.8.summary: David defeats the Philistines and takes their chief city. He defeats Moab and puts two thirds of the captives to death. He defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians of Damascus. He places troops in Syria and Edom, and those peoples serve him. King Toi of Hamath sends gifts of silver, gold, and bronze. David dedicates the metal to the LORD. The LORD gives him victory wherever he goes. The chapter ends with a list of his chief officers.
chapters.8.lds: How does David’s growing rule affect the people his armies defeat?
chapters.9.summary: David asks whether anyone is left from Saul’s house. He wants to show kindness for Jonathan’s sake. Ziba, a servant of Saul’s house, names Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth, who is lame. David sends for him from Lo Debar. Mephibosheth falls on his face before the king. David tells him not to fear and restores all Saul’s land to him. Ziba and his household will farm it. Mephibosheth will eat at the king’s table like one of his sons.
chapters.9.lds: The older manual studies David’s kindness to Jonathan’s son. What does Mephibosheth call himself in verse 8?
chapters.10.summary: The king of Ammon dies, and David sends men to comfort his son Hanun. Hanun’s princes say the visitors are spies. Hanun shaves half of each man’s beard and cuts their clothes at the hips. David lets the shamed men wait at Jericho until their beards grow. Ammon hires Syrian armies. Joab splits his forces with his brother Abishai, and the Syrians flee. Hadadezer brings more Syrians from beyond the River. David defeats them, and they make peace with Israel.
chapters.10.lds: How could Hanun have tested his advisers’ claim before acting?
chapters.11.summary: In spring David sends Joab to besiege Rabbah and stays in Jerusalem. From his roof he sees a woman bathing. She is Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite, one of his soldiers. David sends for her, lies with her, and she becomes pregnant. He calls Uriah home, but Uriah will not go to his house during war. David sends him back with a letter to Joab ordering his death. Uriah is killed at the city wall with other men. David marries Bathsheba, and the thing displeases the LORD.
chapters.11.lds: Come, Follow Me asks readers to examine David's choices and responsibility. Who carries the letter of verse 15 to Joab (verse 14)?
chapters.12.summary: The LORD sends Nathan to David with a story. A rich man took a poor man’s only lamb to feed a guest. David says the man deserves to die. Nathan answers, “You are the man!” The sword will never leave David’s house, and his own wives will be taken. David confesses, and Nathan says he will not die, but the child will. David fasts for seven days until the child dies. Later Bathsheba bears Solomon, and David captures Rabbah.
chapters.12.lds: The older manual compares verse 13 with the Joseph Smith Translation. That version changes Nathan’s words about David’s sin. What does David say about the rich man before verse 7?
chapters.13.summary: David’s son Amnon desires his half sister Tamar. On a cousin’s advice he pretends to be ill and asks her to bring food. He seizes her, and she pleads with him. He rapes her, then hates her and has her thrown out. Tamar tears her royal robe and goes away crying. Her brother Absalom takes her into his house. David is very angry but does nothing. Two years later Absalom has Amnon killed and flees to Geshur.
chapters.13.lds: What does Tamar ask Amnon to do? Who fails to protect her?
chapters.14.summary: Joab sees that David longs for Absalom. He sends a wise woman from Tekoa to the king in mourning clothes. She says one of her sons killed the other in a fight. Her clan now demands the life of the son who is left. David promises to protect him. She then asks why the king does not bring back his own banished son. David guesses that Joab is behind it and lets Absalom return. For two years Absalom may not see the king’s face.
chapters.14.lds: How does Joab use the woman’s story to change David’s decision?
chapters.15.summary: Absalom gets a chariot, horses, and fifty runners. He stands by the gate and meets people who bring cases to the king. He tells each one that his claim is good and no one will hear it. So he steals the hearts of Israel. After four years he goes to Hebron and has himself declared king. David flees Jerusalem with his household and loyal foreign troops. He sends the ark back to the city with the priests. He climbs the Mount of Olives weeping and sends Hushai to act as a spy.
chapters.15.lds: How does Absalom use promises of justice to win support?
chapters.16.summary: Ziba meets the fleeing king with donkeys, bread, fruit, and wine. He says Mephibosheth stayed in Jerusalem hoping to gain Saul’s kingdom. David gives Ziba all of Mephibosheth’s property. At Bahurim a man of Saul’s family named Shimei curses David and throws stones. Abishai wants to cut off his head. David says to leave him; perhaps the LORD told him to curse. Absalom enters Jerusalem, and Hushai pretends to serve him. On Ahithophel’s advice Absalom takes his father’s concubines in public.
chapters.16.lds: Whose account does David hear before giving Ziba the land?
chapters.17.summary: Ahithophel advises Absalom to strike David that night with twelve thousand men. Hushai argues for waiting and gathering all Israel. Absalom prefers Hushai’s advice, as the LORD intended. Hushai sends warning to David through the priests’ two sons. A boy sees them, and they hide in a well at Bahurim. A woman covers the well and sends the searchers away. David crosses the Jordan that night, and Ahithophel hangs himself. At Mahanaim three men bring beds, bowls, and food to David’s people.
chapters.17.lds: Which people bring food and other help to David’s group?
chapters.18.summary: David divides his army under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai. The men will not let him fight. He orders the three to deal gently with Absalom, and all the soldiers hear it. David’s men win in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom’s head catches in an oak, and his mule runs on. A soldier refuses to touch him, but Joab stabs him. Two runners carry the news to the king. David asks only about Absalom and weeps, “My son, my son!”
chapters.18.lds: Why does David’s grief differ from his soldiers’ joy over victory?
chapters.19.summary: Joab tells David that his weeping shames the men who saved him. David sits in the gate, and the people come to him. He invites Judah to bring him back and promises Joab’s post to Amasa. Shimei begs forgiveness at the Jordan, and David spares him. Mephibosheth comes unwashed and says Ziba deceived him. David tells the two to divide the land. Old Barzillai declines a place at court and sends Chimham. Israel and Judah then quarrel over who has more claim to the king.
chapters.19.lds: Which disputes remain after David returns to rule?
chapters.20.summary: Sheba, a man of Benjamin, calls Israel to leave David, and the northern tribes follow. David sets apart the ten concubines Absalom took. Amasa is slow to gather Judah’s army. Joab greets Amasa as a brother and stabs him. Joab’s army besieges Sheba in the town of Abel. A wise woman calls to Joab from the wall. She persuades the town to throw Sheba’s head over to him. Joab withdraws, and a list of David’s officers follows.
chapters.20.lds: The older manual states that David’s concubines were not responsible for Absalom’s violation. What does the woman accuse Joab of in verse 19?
chapters.21.summary: A famine lasts three years, and David asks the LORD why. The answer is that Saul killed Gibeonites, breaking Israel’s old oath. The Gibeonites ask for seven of Saul’s male descendants. David spares Mephibosheth and hands over seven others. They are hanged on a hill at the start of barley harvest. Rizpah, mother of two of them, guards the bodies until the rain comes. David hears of it and buries the bones with Saul’s and Jonathan’s. Four giants later fall to David’s men.
chapters.21.lds: The older manual questions the executions under the law against punishing children for parents’ sins. What does Rizpah do in verse 10?
chapters.22.summary: David sings this song after the LORD rescues him from Saul and all his enemies. He calls the LORD his rock, fortress, and shield. Death’s waves surrounded him, and he cried out. The earth shook, and the LORD came down in storm and fire. He drew David out of deep waters. David says the LORD rewarded his clean hands. With God’s help he can run through a troop and leap a wall. The song ends with kindness to David and his descendants forever.
chapters.22.lds: How does David’s song compare with his choices elsewhere in the book?
chapters.23.summary: David’s last words say a ruler must be just and fear God. Such a ruler is like morning light after rain. God has made a lasting covenant with his house. The chapter then lists David’s mighty men and their deeds. One stood alone in a field and fought until his hand stuck to his sword. Three broke through Philistine lines to bring David water from Bethlehem’s well. Benaiah killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day. The list of the Thirty ends with Uriah the Hittite.
chapters.23.lds: How do the warriors’ actions show the risks of serving a king?
chapters.24.summary: The LORD is angry with Israel, and David is moved to count the people. Joab objects, but the king insists. The count takes almost ten months. Then David’s heart troubles him, and he confesses. The prophet Gad offers three punishments, and David chooses to fall into the LORD’s hand. A plague kills seventy thousand. The angel stops at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. David buys the floor, builds an altar, and the plague ends.
chapters.24.lds: The older Church manual compares this account with First Chronicles 21. Why does David refuse Araunah’s gift in verse 24?
